=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/orchestrate_lib.py
  Line or code reference: 2666
  Problem: The completion-mark regex in `parse_tracking_body` uses `[ x]` (only lowercase `x`), but the existing `TRACKING_BODY_ISSUE_LINE_RE` on line 55 of the same file uses `[ xX]` (both cases). An uppercase `[X]` checkbox — which GitHub's own markdown renderer treats as equivalent to `[x]` — would cause the entire sub-issue line to fail to match entirely, meaning the sub-issue is silently absent from the parsed wave structure rather than being seen as completed or incomplete.
  Why it fails at runtime: If a tracking issue body contains `[X]` (from a manual edit in the GitHub textarea, or a future renderer change), `parse_tracking_body` silently drops the line. `rebuild_tracking_state` then never sees that sub-issue at all, so the `ReconstructionUnsafeError` guard cannot fire — and the from-scratch rebuild proceeds with a truncated view of the project, potentially re-creating the already-completed issue as a duplicate. The existing `TRACKING_BODY_ISSUE_LINE_RE` (line 55) already handles both cases, establishing that case-insensitivity is the intended defensive posture in this file.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: "README.md §13a — document both reconstruction safety guards."
  Expected change site: README.md §13a (the paragraph describing missing-state recovery).
  Evidence of absence: The PR diff does update README.md §13a to describe both guards: (a) the COMMENTS_FETCH_OK precondition and (b) the ReconstructionUnsafeError refusal when completed issues are unmapped. The update is present in the diff at line ~1370, describing both guards in a single sentence appended to the existing paragraph. The pass-1 cross-pollination note suggesting the README update is incomplete because it omits "the new regex named-group capture and the exact refusal/error-message behavior" is asking for implementation-level detail that README-level documentation does not require — the two guard concepts are both documented.
  ALREADY SATISFIED

  Problem: The completion-mark capture group only matches literal space or lowercase `x`, while the established tracking-body regex `TRACKING_BODY_ISSUE_LINE_RE` at line 54 accepts `[ xX]` (both cases). If a tracking issue body ever contains `[X]` — whether from manual operator edits, future rendering changes, or third-party tooling — the mark will not be recognized as completed. `issue.get("completed")` will return `False`, and `rebuild_tracking_state` will not raise `ReconstructionUnsafeError` for that sub-issue.
  Why it fails at runtime: A project with `[X]`-marked completions and an empty/unparseable issue map would proceed through reconstruction instead of being refused, resetting `current_wave` to 1 and potentially creating duplicate issues for already-completed work — the exact #3627 failure mode this PR is meant to prevent. The fix is a one-character change: `[ x]` → `[ xX]`.
